bull.b: A $2.7 billion contracted backlog provides substantial multi-year revenue visibility and supports capacity planning. The stated 2027 deployment path, combined with recurring revenue from live projects, gives the business a foundation for sustained scaling beyond individual quarterly bookings.

bull.t: Strong Gross Economics And Improving Operating Performance
bull.b: Very high gross margins indicate attractive unit economics, while positive adjusted EBITDA suggests operating performance is improving as deployments scale. If these economics persist, incremental revenue can contribute more meaningfully to cash generation and support continued infrastructure expansion.

bull.t: Diversified Customer Base And Long-term Contracts
bull.b: Customer diversity reduces reliance on any single end market or account and broadens the company’s opportunity across expanding AI infrastructure use cases. Long-term contracts with varied customers can improve revenue durability while supporting repeat deployments and expansion opportunities.

bear.b: Material net losses show that rapid revenue growth has not yet translated into bottom-line profitability. Continued losses can consume financial resources, limit internally funded expansion, and make the company more dependent on successful deployment execution and external project financing.

bear.t: High Leverage And Rising Financing Obligations
bear.b: High leverage materially reduces financial flexibility and increases sensitivity to execution problems or weaker cash generation. Rising GPU finance lease payments add a growing fixed obligation, which can absorb cash that would otherwise support expansion, reserves, or progress toward profitability.

bear.t: Cash Flow Quality And Project Timing Risk
bear.b: Reported operating cash flow was heavily supported by customer deposits and payables, so quarterly cash generation may not represent sustainable operating earnings. Project timing delays can also defer recurring revenue and cash inflows, complicating liquidity planning during rapid capacity expansion.
